title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
summary: Book 1 of the Oz series (1900). Follow Dorothy from Kansas to Oz, on to the Emerald City, the Wicked Witch's castle and Glinda's castle, then home again. Pass each of the 24 chapters as you read it, then take the whole-book test at the end. Explores courage, kindness, wisdom, appearances versus reality, and the meaning of home.

questions.q: Where does Dorothy live at the start of the story?
options: On a farm on the Kansas prairies
In a city apartment in Omaha
In a cabin in the mountains
questions.why: She lives in the middle of the great Kansas prairies with Uncle Henry and Aunt Em.

questions.q: What is Uncle Henry's job?
questions.why: Uncle Henry is a farmer, which is why he runs to look after the stock when the storm comes.

questions.q: How many rooms does the house have?
questions.why: The house is a single room with four walls, a floor and a roof — small because lumber had to be carried by wagon from far away.

questions.q: What is the only 'cellar' the family has?
options: A root cellar under the barn
A storm cave in a hillside
A small cyclone cellar reached by a trapdoor in the floor
questions.why: The cyclone cellar is a hole dug in the ground, reached by a trapdoor and ladder — built for exactly this kind of storm.

questions.q: Which color does the narrator use again and again to describe Kansas and the people in it?
questions.why: Prairie, house, Aunt Em and Uncle Henry are all gray. This sets up a sharp contrast with the bright colors of Oz.

questions.q: How has life on the prairie changed Aunt Em?
options: It made her cheerful and plump
The sun and wind took the sparkle from her eyes and the red from her cheeks
It made her quick to laugh
It made her afraid of dogs
questions.why: She arrived young and pretty, but the harsh land wore the color and joy out of her.

questions.q: What does Aunt Em do when Dorothy's laughter first reaches her?
options: She screams and presses her hand to her heart
questions.why: Aunt Em was so unused to laughter that the sound of it startled her.

questions.q: According to the narrator, what keeps Dorothy from growing as gray as everything around her?
questions.why: Toto, the little black dog, is what saved her from growing gray. He is a real anchor of joy in her life.

questions.q: How is Toto described?
options: A little black dog with long silky hair and small black eyes
A white terrier with a curly tail
A spotted puppy with floppy ears
questions.why: This detail matters later: Toto is small and quick enough to cause trouble at key moments.

questions.q: What first warns Uncle Henry that a storm is coming?
options: A low wail of the wind from the north, and the long grass bowing in waves
The animals run into the house
questions.why: He hears the wind from the north and then sees ripples in the grass from the south — two winds that will meet.

questions.q: Where does Uncle Henry go when the storm comes?
options: To the sheds to look after the cows and horses
questions.why: He runs to the stock, leaving Aunt Em to call Dorothy to the cellar.

questions.q: Why doesn't Dorothy get into the cellar in time?
options: Toto jumps out of her arms and hides under the bed, and she goes after him
questions.why: Dorothy won't leave Toto behind. Her loyalty is what keeps her in the house.

questions.q: Why does the house end up in the very center of the cyclone?
options: The north and south winds meet where the house stands
The house is the tallest thing around
A witch's spell pulls it there
Uncle Henry built it on a hill
questions.why: Because two winds meet at that spot, the house lands in the calm middle of the storm and is carried away whole.

questions.q: How does the narrator describe the house being carried through the air?
options: Like a stone thrown from a sling
As easily as you could carry a feather
Like a ship in a storm, crashing up and down
questions.why: The house rises to the top of the cyclone and is carried along as lightly as a feather.

questions.q: What happens to Toto during the flight?
options: He runs out the front door
He hides in the cupboard for the whole trip
He falls through the open trapdoor, and Dorothy pulls him back by his ear
He falls asleep under the table
questions.why: The strong air pressure holds Toto up in the opening, so Dorothy can grab him and then close the trapdoor.

questions.q: What does Dorothy do to prevent another accident after rescuing Toto?
questions.why: She shuts the trapdoor so no one else can fall through.

questions.q: How does Dorothy's fear change as the hours pass?
options: She grows calm and decides to wait and see what happens
She grows more terrified and screams the whole time
She prays the house will land in Kansas
questions.why: She feels lonely at first, but her fear fades as nothing bad happens. It shows her steady, practical nature.

questions.q: What does Dorothy finally do while the house is still in the air?
options: Writes a letter to Aunt Em
Crawls to her bed, lies down, and falls asleep with Toto beside her
Watches out of the window all night
questions.why: Despite the swaying and the wailing wind, she sleeps. Chapter 2 begins with her waking up.

questions.q: What does the house's rising out of gray Kansas suggest about the story to come?
options: Dorothy will never want to go home
Kansas is a dangerous, evil place
Dorothy is being carried out of an ordinary, colorless world into an unknown one
The story will be about farming
questions.why: The chapter sets up a journey away from a gray, familiar world — and her wish to return is still the heart of the book.

questions.q: Which word best describes Dorothy's choice to go after Toto instead of hurrying to safety?
questions.why: She puts her friend's safety ahead of her own. This loyalty shows up again and again in the book.

questions.q: What wakes Dorothy up?
options: A sudden, severe shock as the house lands
questions.why: The house comes down with a jolt. The soft bed keeps her from getting hurt.

questions.q: How is the land outside different from Kansas?
options: It is also gray and flat
It is a lovely country of green grass, fruit trees, flowers, birds and a brook
questions.why: The bright, beautiful land is the opposite of the gray prairie.

questions.q: What is unusual about the three men's hats?
options: They are round, rise to a point a foot above their heads, and have little bells around the brims
questions.why: The bells tinkle as the men move. The men are dressed in blue, the Munchkin color.

questions.q: How does the old woman greet Dorothy?
questions.why: She welcomes Dorothy to the land of the Munchkins and thanks her for killing the Wicked Witch of the East.

questions.q: How does Dorothy respond to being thanked for killing the Witch?
options: She says she has not killed anything
questions.why: Dorothy is honest and confused. The woman replies that her house did it anyway.

questions.q: What is sticking out from under the corner of the house?
options: Two feet in silver shoes with pointed toes
questions.why: Those feet belong to the Wicked Witch of the East, who was crushed when the house landed.

questions.q: What had the Wicked Witch of the East done to the Munchkins?
options: She kept them in bondage, making them her slaves day and night
questions.why: Her death sets the Munchkins free, which is why they are so grateful.

questions.q: Who is the old woman?
options: The Wicked Witch of the West
Glinda, the Witch of the South
questions.why: She is a good witch, though she says she is not as powerful as the Wicked Witch of the East was.

questions.q: How many witches does the Witch of the North say there are in the Land of Oz?
questions.why: There are four: the witches of the North and South are good, and those of the East and West are wicked.

questions.q: Why does the Witch of the North think Kansas has no witches?
options: Kansas is a civilized country, and she believes civilized countries have no witches or wizards left
questions.why: She explains that Oz has never been civilized because it is cut off from the rest of the world.

questions.q: What happens to the dead witch's body?
options: It dries up quickly in the sun, leaving only the silver shoes
questions.why: She was so old that she dried up in the sun — only her shoes remain.

questions.q: What do the Munchkins say about the silver shoes?
options: They are made of real emeralds
The witch was proud of them, and there is some charm connected with them, but no one knows what it is
questions.why: This is a hint planted early. The shoes' power isn't explained until the end of the book.

questions.q: What does the land that surrounds Oz on every side consist of?
options: A great desert that no one can cross
questions.why: The desert is why Dorothy can't simply walk home.

questions.q: What does Dorothy do when she learns she can't easily get home?
options: She begins to cry, and the kind Munchkins cry too
She gets angry at the witch
questions.why: The Munchkins' tender hearts make them weep along with her.

questions.q: How does the Witch of the North try to find an answer for Dorothy?
options: She balances her cap on her nose and counts one, two, three, and it becomes a slate with a message
She looks into a crystal ball
She reads a book of spells
questions.why: The slate reads, in chalk, 'LET DOROTHY GO TO THE CITY OF EMERALDS.'

questions.q: Who does the Witch of the North say is more powerful than all the other witches together?
options: The Queen of the Field Mice
questions.why: She sends Dorothy to Oz in the City of Emeralds, in the center of the country.

questions.q: What gift does the Witch of the North give Dorothy for protection?
options: Her kiss on the forehead, which leaves a round, shining mark
questions.why: No one will dare harm someone the Witch of the North has kissed. The mark matters again later.

questions.q: How will Dorothy find the way to the City of Emeralds?
options: By following the road paved with yellow brick
questions.why: The yellow brick road leads straight to the city.

questions.q: How does the Witch of the North leave?
options: She turns around three times on her left heel and vanishes
She flies off on a broom
She rides away in a bubble
questions.why: She disappears on the spot, which surprises Toto so much that he barks.

questions.q: Why does Dorothy's arrival seem so lucky to the Munchkins but confusing to her?
options: She freed a whole people by accident and doesn't feel she did anything
She wanted to be a witch
She knew the witch from Kansas
questions.why: Dorothy is honored as a heroine for something she didn't choose to do. Her modesty sets her apart from the powerful figures of Oz.

questions.q: What dress does Dorothy change into before her journey?
options: A clean gingham dress with checks of white and blue
questions.why: The blue and white checks matter later, when Boq reads meaning into them.

questions.q: Why does Dorothy put on the silver shoes?
options: Her old shoes are worn out, and the silver ones fit her
The Witch of the North ordered her to
questions.why: She takes them for a practical reason. She has no idea of their power yet.

questions.q: What does Dorothy carry with her on the road?
options: A basket filled with bread, covered with a white cloth
questions.why: Food is a real worry for Dorothy throughout the early chapters.

questions.q: What shape are the Munchkins' houses?
options: Round, with big domes for roofs
questions.why: The houses are painted blue, the favorite color of the East.

questions.q: How do the Munchkins treat Dorothy as she passes?
options: They come out and bow low, because she destroyed the Wicked Witch
questions.why: Her fame has spread, and people treat her with gratitude.

questions.q: Who is Boq?
options: One of the richest Munchkins, who is holding a feast
A farmer who made the Scarecrow
A soldier in the Emerald City
questions.why: The Munchkins are celebrating their freedom at his house, and Dorothy spends the night there.

questions.q: Why does Boq decide Dorothy must be a great sorceress?
options: She wears silver shoes and killed the Wicked Witch
questions.why: He reads power into her shoes and her deed.

questions.q: Why does Boq think Dorothy is a friendly witch?
options: Because her dress has white in it, and only witches and sorceresses wear white
questions.why: Blue is the Munchkin color and white is the witch color, so her blue-and-white dress seems like a sign that she is friendly.

questions.q: Where does Dorothy find the Scarecrow?
options: Stuck up on a pole in a cornfield, to keep the birds away from the ripe corn
questions.why: He is there to scare crows.

questions.q: How is the Scarecrow's head made?
options: Made of cloth stuffed with feathers
A small sack stuffed with straw, with eyes, nose and mouth painted on
questions.why: His painted face is what makes Dorothy notice him — especially when one eye winks.

questions.q: What first shows Dorothy that the Scarecrow is alive?
options: One of his painted eyes slowly winks at her
questions.why: She thinks she must be mistaken, since Kansas scarecrows never wink.

questions.q: How does Dorothy free the Scarecrow?
options: She lifts him off the pole, which is easy because he is light and stuffed with straw
She cuts the ropes with a knife
questions.why: He is so light that she can lift him easily.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow want to go with Dorothy?
questions.why: He says he has no brains at all because his head is stuffed with straw.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow say he doesn't mind being stuffed?
options: It makes him light enough to fly
He can't get hurt — if someone steps on his toes he won't feel it
questions.why: His body can't be hurt, but he does not want people to call him a fool.

questions.q: What is the one thing the Scarecrow is afraid of?
questions.why: Fire is the only real danger to a man of straw. It foreshadows how carefully he stays away from the campfire later.

questions.q: When the Scarecrow asks whether Oz will give him brains, what does Dorothy point out?
options: If Oz won't, he will be no worse off than he is now
He should stay on his pole instead
Only the Witch of the North can give brains
questions.why: Dorothy can't promise anything, but she sees that he has nothing to lose by coming.

questions.q: What is on the Scarecrow's head?
options: An old, pointed blue hat that had belonged to some Munchkin
questions.why: Even the Scarecrow is dressed in Munchkin blue.

questions.q: How does Toto first react to the Scarecrow?
options: He sniffs around him suspiciously and growls at first
questions.why: Toto isn't sure what to make of a man of straw.

questions.q: What irony is set up in this chapter about the Scarecrow and brains?
options: He is already foolish in every way
He wants to be a crow
He speaks thoughtfully about himself while claiming he has no brains
questions.why: The Scarecrow reasons clearly while saying he can't think. The book keeps showing that he already has what he is looking for.

questions.q: Where does the chapter end?
options: Dorothy and the Scarecrow walking along the yellow brick road together
questions.why: They set off together toward the Emerald City.

questions.q: What happens to the road after a few hours?
options: It gets rough, and the Scarecrow keeps stumbling over the yellow bricks and falling into holes
questions.why: Dorothy walks around the holes and Toto jumps over them, but the Scarecrow walks straight into them.

questions.q: Why doesn't falling hurt the Scarecrow?
options: He is stuffed with straw, so he doesn't feel it
questions.why: Dorothy simply picks him up and sets him on his feet again.

questions.q: How does the countryside change as they walk?
options: The farms are not so well cared for, and there are fewer houses and fruit trees
questions.why: The land becomes lonelier and wilder as they move toward the forest.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow say he is never hungry?
options: His mouth is only painted, and cutting a hole to eat through would let his straw out
questions.why: Eating would change the shape of his head.

questions.q: What does Dorothy tell the Scarecrow about Kansas?
options: That it is full of gold
That it is gray and dry
That it is green and rainy
That it is ruled by a king
questions.why: She describes the gray prairie and the cyclone that carried her away.

questions.q: Why can't the Scarecrow understand Dorothy's wish to go back?
options: He has never heard of Kansas
He doesn't see why anyone would leave this beautiful country for a dry, gray place
He wants her to be his servant
questions.why: He can't understand her longing without having a home of his own.

questions.q: How does Dorothy explain wanting to go home?
options: People of flesh and blood would rather live at home, however gray, because there is no place like home
questions.why: This is one of the book's central ideas: home matters more than beauty.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow say is lucky for Kansas?
options: That it is far from Oz
questions.why: He jokes that if people's heads were stuffed with straw like his, they'd all live in the beautiful places and Kansas would have no people at all.

questions.q: How long ago was the Scarecrow made?
questions.why: Being so new, he knows almost nothing about the world.

questions.q: What is the first thing the farmer painted on the Scarecrow?
questions.why: Because his ears were painted first, the Scarecrow could hear the farmer before he could see anything.

questions.q: What color did the farmer think was just right for eyes?
questions.why: He comments that blue paint is just the color for eyes.

questions.q: What happened when the farmer put the Scarecrow on the pole?
options: He felt lonely after being left alone, and soon the crows stopped being afraid of him
He scared all the crows away forever
questions.why: At first birds fly away, but an old crow sees that he is only stuffed with straw.

questions.q: What did the old crow tell the Scarecrow?
options: That brains are the only things worth having, whether one is a crow or a man
questions.why: This advice is what gives the Scarecrow his goal.

questions.q: How does the old crow's advice affect the Scarecrow?
options: He decides to try hard to get some brains
He decides to become a crow
questions.why: It sets his quest in motion before Dorothy arrives.

questions.q: What is it like when the travelers reach the forest?
options: The trees are so big and close together that their branches block out the daylight
questions.why: Darkness falls quickly under the trees.

questions.q: How does Dorothy manage to walk in the dark?
options: She holds on to the Scarecrow's arm
questions.why: She can hardly see, so she holds on to the Scarecrow as they go.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow find for Dorothy to sleep in?
options: A little cottage built of logs and branches
questions.why: Dorothy finds a bed of dried leaves in one corner.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow do while Dorothy sleeps?
options: He goes to look for food
He stands up in another corner and waits patiently until morning
questions.why: He never gets tired, so he needs no sleep.

questions.q: Which word best describes the Scarecrow in this chapter?
questions.why: He guides Dorothy through the dark, finds her shelter, and keeps watch. His kindness and good sense show even without brains.

questions.q: What is this chapter's main idea about home?
options: A home is valuable for the love and belonging it gives, not for how it looks
questions.why: Dorothy's longing for plain, gray Kansas shows that home is about belonging, not beauty.

chapters.title: 5. The Rescue of the Tin Woodman

questions.q: What does Dorothy look for when she wakes up in the cottage?
options: Water, to wash her face and drink
A way out of the forest
questions.why: She finds a little spring of clear water and eats breakfast beside it.

questions.q: What worries Dorothy about her food?
options: There is not much bread left in the basket
questions.why: The Scarecrow is glad he doesn't need to eat, since it seems like a lot of trouble.

questions.q: What sound leads them to the Tin Woodman?
questions.why: The groaning comes from a man of tin standing stock-still in the forest.

questions.q: In what position is the Tin Woodman found?
options: Holding his axe raised in the air, standing perfectly still
questions.why: He has been frozen in the middle of a chop.

questions.q: How long has the Tin Woodman been groaning with no one to help him?
questions.why: He says that no one had heard him or come to help him in all that time.

questions.q: Why can't the Tin Woodman move?
options: A witch froze him in place
questions.why: He was caught in the rain, and now his joints are rusted stiff.

questions.q: Where does Dorothy find the oil-can?
options: On a shelf in the Tin Woodman's cottage
questions.why: It turns out the cottage where Dorothy slept was his home.

questions.q: Which joint does Dorothy oil first?
questions.why: Once his neck works, the Scarecrow moves his head from side to side until it is free. Then she oils his arms and legs.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman do as soon as his arms are free?
options: Lowers his axe with a sigh and leans it against a tree
questions.why: He has been holding that axe up the whole time he was rusted.

questions.q: Who put the enchantment on the Tin Woodman's axe?
options: The Wicked Witch of the West
The Wicked Witch of the East
questions.why: The witch who died under Dorothy's house is the one who caused his troubles.

questions.q: What did the enchanted axe do?
options: It turned him to tin all at once
It slipped and cut off parts of his body one after another
questions.why: Each time, a tinsmith replaced the lost part with tin, until he was made entirely of tin.

questions.q: Which part of him did the axe cut off first?
questions.why: The legs went first, then the arms, then the head, and finally his body was split in two.

questions.q: Who replaced each lost part with tin?
options: The farmer who made the Scarecrow
questions.why: Each tin part helped the woodman keep working, but the new body had no heart.

questions.q: What did the Tin Woodman lose when his body was replaced with tin?
questions.why: Without a heart, he says, he could no longer love or care the way he used to.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman say was the only danger to his tin body?
questions.why: He kept an oil-can in his cottage, but once he forgot it and was caught in a rainstorm.

questions.q: What did the Tin Woodman decide during his year of standing still?
options: That the greatest loss he had known was the loss of his heart
That he would get revenge on the Witch
That he wanted to be a king
questions.why: Being stuck gave him time to think about what matters most.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman ask Dorothy to do with the oil-can?
options: Put it in her basket, in case he gets caught in the rain again
Give it to the Scarecrow to wear
questions.why: Carrying the oil-can pays off very soon, in the next chapter.

questions.q: Why does the Tin Woodman say he will ask for a heart, not brains?
options: Brains do not make one happy, and happiness is the best thing in the world
questions.why: He and the Scarecrow each believe that what they lack is the most important thing.

questions.q: How does the Scarecrow answer?
options: He agrees and wants a heart too
He says he doesn't want anything
He says he'll ask for brains, because a fool wouldn't know what to do with a heart
questions.why: The friendly debate between heart and brains runs through the whole book.

questions.q: How does the Tin Woodman help the group as they travel on?
options: He chops away branches that block the road
questions.why: His axe clears the path through the thick forest.

questions.q: What is the road like at the start of this chapter?
options: Covered with dry branches and dead leaves, in a thick forest
questions.why: The forest is dark and gloomy, and they hear the growls of wild animals.

questions.q: What does the Lion do to the Scarecrow?
options: Knocks him spinning to the edge of the road with one blow of his paw
questions.why: The Scarecrow is so light that he goes flying.

questions.q: What happens when the Lion strikes the Tin Woodman with his claws?
options: The Woodman falls over, but the tin isn't marked
questions.why: The Lion's claws can't scratch tin, which surprises him.

questions.q: What does Dorothy do when the Lion opens his mouth to bite Toto?
options: She slaps the Lion on the nose and scolds him
questions.why: She acts without thinking about her own danger, and it takes the fight out of the Lion.

questions.q: What does Dorothy call the Lion?
questions.why: The Lion hangs his head in shame and admits that it is true.

questions.q: Why does the Lion say that other animals expect him to be brave?
options: He is the biggest animal in the forest
The Lion is thought everywhere to be the King of Beasts
questions.why: He feels the pressure of being expected to be something he isn't.

questions.q: How has the Lion managed to hide his cowardice?
options: By roaring loudly, which frightens other creatures away
questions.why: His roar is a bluff. He admits that if an elephant or tiger ever fought him, he would run.

questions.q: Why did the Scarecrow go over so easily, according to the Lion?
questions.why: The Lion is amazed to learn what the Scarecrow is made of.

questions.q: When the Lion asks whether Toto is made of tin or stuffed, what does Dorothy answer?
options: Neither — he is a meat dog
questions.why: The Lion then says that no one would think of biting something so small, except a coward like himself.

questions.q: What happens to the Lion's heart whenever there is danger?
questions.why: This leads to the Tin Woodman's comment about heart disease.

questions.q: Why does the Tin Woodman say the Lion should be glad if he has heart disease?
options: It proves that he has a heart
questions.why: The Woodman wants a heart so much that even a sick one sounds like a gift.

questions.q: What does the Lion wonder about having no heart?
options: Whether he would not be a coward if he had no heart
questions.why: Each character sees his own problem in a different way.

questions.q: Why does the Lion decide to join the group?
options: To ask Oz to give him courage
To become king of the Emerald City
questions.why: He says his life is simply unbearable without courage.

questions.q: How does the Lion help the group once he joins?
options: His roaring keeps other wild animals away
questions.why: Even a cowardly lion scares off other creatures.

questions.q: How does Toto feel about the Lion at first?
options: He barks at him all day
He doesn't approve of him, remembering how nearly he was crushed
questions.why: Toto is slow to forgive, but he gets used to the Lion.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman accidentally do on the road?
options: Steps on a beetle and kills it
questions.why: He is very upset about it, because he tries not to hurt any living creature.

questions.q: Why can't the Tin Woodman speak after this?
options: He is too sad to talk
His tears rust his jaws together
questions.why: His tears run down his face and rust the hinges of his jaw.

questions.q: Who fixes the Tin Woodman's jaws?
options: The Scarecrow, with the oil-can from Dorothy's basket
questions.why: Carrying the oil-can pays off right away.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman say about people who have hearts?
options: They have something to guide them and need never do wrong
questions.why: Because he has no heart, he feels he must be very careful never to be cruel.

questions.q: What does the beetle incident suggest about the Tin Woodman?
options: He already has a kind, caring heart, even though he thinks he doesn't
questions.why: He cries over a beetle. His kindness shows that he already has what he is looking for.

chapters.title: 7. The Journey to the Great Oz

questions.q: Where do the travelers spend the first night after the Lion joins them?
options: Under a large tree in the forest
questions.why: There is no house nearby, so they camp outdoors.

questions.q: Who chops wood for the fire?
questions.why: Dorothy builds the fire from the wood he chops.

questions.q: What does the Lion offer to do for Dorothy's supper?
options: Go into the forest and kill a deer for her to roast
questions.why: The Tin Woodman begs him not to, because he would cry for the deer and rust his jaws.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow gather for Dorothy?
options: Nuts, which he puts in her basket
questions.why: His padded hands are clumsy, so he drops many nuts, but he fills the basket so Dorothy won't be hungry.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow stay away from the fire?
options: He is afraid a spark might get into his straw and burn him up
questions.why: This connects back to his fear of a lighted match.

questions.q: What blocks the road the next morning?
options: A great ditch that divides the forest, with jagged rocks at the bottom
questions.why: The sides are too steep to climb down.

questions.q: Who solves the problem of the first ditch?
options: The Tin Woodman, with his axe
The Lion, who thinks he can jump over it
questions.why: The Scarecrow then realizes the Lion can carry them across one at a time.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow insist on going first?
options: If the Lion fails, the fall won't hurt a straw man
He wants to see the other side first
questions.why: He reasons that a fall would kill Dorothy or badly dent the Tin Woodman, but wouldn't hurt him at all.

questions.q: What does the Lion admit before jumping?
options: He is terribly afraid of falling himself
questions.why: He is afraid, but he does it anyway. This shows the courage he thinks he lacks.

questions.q: In what order does the Lion carry the travelers across the first ditch?
options: Scarecrow, then Dorothy with Toto, then the Tin Woodman
questions.why: The Scarecrow goes first as a test, then Dorothy holding Toto, then the Tin Woodman.

questions.q: What are the Kalidahs?
options: Monstrous beasts with bodies like bears and heads like tigers
questions.why: The Lion is terribly afraid of them. He says their claws could tear him in two.

questions.q: Why can't the Lion jump the second ditch?
options: It is much broader and deeper
questions.why: The Lion can tell at once that the gap is too wide for him.

questions.q: What is the Scarecrow's plan for the second ditch?
options: Have the Tin Woodman chop down a tree so it falls across the ditch as a bridge
questions.why: The Lion jokes that you'd almost think the Scarecrow had brains in his head.

questions.q: How many Kalidahs chase them across the tree?
questions.why: Two Kalidahs come after them.

questions.q: What does the Lion do when the Kalidahs appear?
options: Turns and gives a terrible roar, then says he will fight them as long as he is alive
questions.why: Even while afraid, he stands in front of his friends. His actions say more than his words.

questions.q: How are the Kalidahs defeated?
options: The Tin Woodman chops through the end of the tree, and they fall into the gulf
questions.why: The Scarecrow thinks of it. Brains and teamwork win where strength could not.

questions.q: What stops the travelers after they leave the forest?
questions.why: On the other side they can see a beautiful country of green meadows.

questions.q: How do they plan to cross the river?
options: Ride on a raft that the Tin Woodman builds
Wait for the water to go down
questions.why: The raft isn't finished by nightfall, so they sleep first.

questions.q: What does Dorothy dream about that night?
options: The Emerald City and the good Wizard Oz, who will soon send her home
questions.why: The dream shows what she is hoping for.

questions.q: What does this chapter show about the Lion?
options: He acts bravely even while he feels afraid
questions.why: He jumps the ditch and faces the Kalidahs while afraid. Courage is doing the right thing in spite of fear.

questions.q: Where does Dorothy sit on the raft?
questions.why: The Lion's weight tips the raft, so the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman stand at the other end to balance it.

questions.q: What goes wrong on the river?
options: The swift current carries the raft downstream, away from the yellow brick road
questions.why: The deep water is too strong for their poles.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman fear will happen if they can't land?
options: They'll be carried into the Wicked Witch of the West's country and made her slaves
questions.why: Each friend then names what he would lose: brains, courage, a heart, or the way home.

questions.q: What happens to the Scarecrow?
options: His pole sticks in the mud, and he is left clinging to it in the middle of the river
He falls into the water and floats away
He is eaten by a fish
questions.why: He pushes his pole in so hard that it sticks, and the raft is swept away from under him.

questions.q: How does the Scarecrow feel stuck on the pole?
options: Worse off than when he first met Dorothy
questions.why: Being stuck on a pole in a river seems even worse than being stuck on a pole in a cornfield.

questions.q: How do the others get the raft to shore?
options: The Lion swims and tows the raft behind him
questions.why: The Tin Woodman holds on to the Lion's tail while the Lion swims for shore.

questions.q: Where are they when they finally land?
options: Right beside the yellow brick road
questions.why: They have to walk back along the bank to find the road again.

questions.q: Who rescues the Scarecrow?
questions.why: She stops to talk while flying past and offers to help.

questions.q: What condition does the Stork give for helping?
options: If the Scarecrow is too heavy to carry, she'll have to drop him back in the river
They must give her the oil-can
questions.why: Dorothy assures her he's stuffed with straw and not heavy at all.

questions.q: Why does the Stork have to leave quickly?
options: Her babies are waiting for her in the nest
She is afraid of the Lion
questions.why: She is kind but has her own family to care for.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow promise after he is rescued?
options: To give the Stork his hat
Never to go near water again
To find the Stork and do her a kindness if he ever gets brains
questions.why: He wants to repay her kindness.

questions.q: What color are the poppies?
questions.why: The great beds of scarlet poppies are so bright that they almost dazzle Dorothy's eyes.

questions.q: What does the narrator say is the danger of the poppies?
options: When many grow together, their smell makes anyone who breathes it fall asleep — and sleep forever unless carried away
They belong to the Wicked Witch
questions.why: Dorothy doesn't know this, which is what makes the field so dangerous.

questions.q: Which travelers are NOT affected by the poppies?
options: The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman
questions.why: They are not made of flesh, so the scent doesn't affect them.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow tell the Lion to do?
options: Run as fast as he can and get out of the flower bed
questions.why: The Lion is too big for them to carry, so his only hope is to get out on his own.

questions.q: How do the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman carry Dorothy?
options: They make a chair with their hands and arms and carry her between them, with Toto on her lap
They drag her on a raft
The Scarecrow carries her on his back
questions.why: They work together to carry her through the field.

questions.q: What do they find partway through the poppy field?
options: The Lion, fast asleep among the poppies
questions.why: The scent was too strong for him, and he fell asleep just before the edge of the field.

questions.q: Why do they leave the Lion behind?
options: He is much too heavy to lift
questions.why: They are sad, thinking he will sleep forever.

questions.q: As they leave him, what do his friends hope the sleeping Lion might dream of?
options: That he has found courage at last
questions.why: It is a gentle, sad farewell.

questions.q: Where do they lay Dorothy?
options: On the soft grass by the river, far enough from the poppies
questions.why: They wait there for the fresh air to wake her.

chapters.title: 9. The Queen of the Field Mice

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman see chasing something through the grass?
questions.why: The Wildcat is chasing a little gray field mouse.

questions.q: Why does the Tin Woodman kill the Wildcat even though he has no heart?
options: He thinks it is wrong to kill such a pretty, harmless creature as the mouse
questions.why: He acts to protect the weak — more evidence of his hidden kindness.

questions.q: Who is the little mouse?
options: The Queen of all the Field Mice
questions.why: She is grateful to the Tin Woodman for saving her life.

questions.q: How does the mouse describe the Tin Woodman's act?
options: A great deed, as well as a brave one
questions.why: Her subjects arrive, and she tells them how he saved her.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow ask the mice to do?
options: Rescue the Lion from the poppy field
questions.why: His quick thinking turns a lucky meeting into a rescue plan.

questions.q: What worries the Queen about the plan?
options: The poppies will put the mice to sleep
The Lion is too far away
The Tin Woodman might hurt them
questions.why: The Scarecrow assures her that this Lion is a coward.

questions.q: What must each mouse bring?
questions.why: The strings will be used to harness the mice to the truck.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman build?
options: A truck from tree limbs, with wheels cut from a tree trunk
questions.why: He makes a cart that can hold the heavy Lion.

questions.q: About how many mice come to help?
questions.why: Mice come from every direction, big and small.

questions.q: How are the mice attached to the truck?
options: Each mouse is tied to the truck by one end of a string, the other end around its neck
questions.why: Once harnessed, the whole crowd of mice can pull together.

questions.q: What happens to Dorothy while the truck is being built?
options: She wakes up and is surprised to find herself surrounded by mice
She goes to find the road
questions.why: The Scarecrow explains what is going on, and she greets the Queen.

questions.q: How do the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman help move the Lion?
options: They carry him on their backs
They lift him onto the truck and push from behind while the mice pull
questions.why: It is a team effort between the biggest and smallest helpers.

questions.q: Why can the mice pull the Lion when the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman could not carry him alone?
options: Many small helpers working together can do what a few cannot
The Lion gets lighter while asleep
questions.why: This is one of the book's clearest lessons about teamwork.

questions.q: Where do they take the Lion?
options: Out of the poppies to the green fields, where he can breathe fresh air
questions.why: Fresh air, away from the poppy scent, will eventually wake him.

questions.q: What does the Queen promise before leaving?
options: That if they ever need her again, they can come out into the field and call, and the mice will come
To fight the Wicked Witch for them
questions.why: Her promise matters later in the story.

questions.q: What does Dorothy eat while waiting for the Lion to wake?
options: Fruit that the Scarecrow picks from a nearby tree
questions.why: Her bread is nearly gone, so the Scarecrow finds food for her.

questions.q: How does the Tin Woodman's rescue of the mouse end up helping the Lion?
options: The mouse he saved is the Queen, whose subjects then rescue the Lion
The Wildcat was guarding the Lion
questions.why: One kind act leads to another.

questions.q: What does the Wildcat have that the narrator notices as it chases the mouse?
options: Its mouth open, showing two rows of ugly teeth, and red eyes glowing
questions.why: The description makes it clear how helpless the mouse was.

questions.q: How does the Queen treat Dorothy?
options: Politely and kindly, speaking with her like a friend
questions.why: Dorothy greets her politely too.

questions.q: What lesson does this chapter teach about size?
options: Even the smallest creatures can do great things
questions.why: The Lion himself notices later that such small animals saved his life.

questions.q: How does the Lion feel when he wakes up?
options: Glad to be alive, and amazed that mice saved him
Ready to go back to the poppies
questions.why: He can't believe such small animals saved his life.

questions.q: How do the travelers find the yellow brick road again?
options: They walk until they reach it
questions.why: Once rested, they set out through the fields and find the road again.

questions.q: What color are the fences and houses as they get closer to the Emerald City?
questions.why: The changing colors show that they are entering a new part of Oz.

questions.q: How do the people in this area react to the travelers?
options: They keep away, afraid of the Lion
questions.why: No one comes near them because of the great Lion.

questions.q: Where do the travelers spend the night?
options: In a farmhouse, where a woman lets them in
questions.why: The woman agrees after Dorothy explains that the Lion is tame and a coward.

questions.q: Who else is in the farmhouse?
options: A man with a hurt leg
questions.why: He tells them what he knows about Oz.

questions.q: What does the man say about seeing Oz?
options: Oz never lets anyone come into his presence
questions.why: He has never seen Oz himself.

questions.q: What does the man say about Oz's appearance?
options: He is a tall wizard with a beard
He is a small old man
He can take any form he wishes, so no one knows what he really looks like
questions.why: Some say he appears as a bird, an elephant, or a cat. This is a hint of the tricks to come.

questions.q: What does the man say Oz has for the Scarecrow?
questions.why: He also says Oz has many hearts and a great pot of courage.

questions.q: Where does the man say Oz keeps a great pot of courage?
questions.why: He says it is covered with a golden plate to keep it from running over.

questions.q: What surrounds the Emerald City?
options: A high, thick wall, bright green in color
questions.why: Its glow is visible from far away.

questions.q: How do the travelers get the gate opened?
options: Dorothy rings a bell beside the gate
questions.why: The gate swings open onto a room with a high arched roof.

questions.q: What does the Guardian of the Gates look like?
options: A little man about the size of the Munchkins, dressed all in green
A soldier with a long beard
questions.why: Even his skin is greenish.

questions.q: What is the Guardian's warning about Oz?
options: Oz is powerful and terrible, and might destroy anyone who comes on a foolish errand
questions.why: He still agrees to take them to the palace.

questions.q: What must everyone wear in the Emerald City?
questions.why: The Guardian says the city's brightness and glory would blind them otherwise.

questions.q: How are the spectacles kept on?
options: With golden bands locked at the back by a key
questions.why: The Guardian keeps the key on a chain around his neck.

questions.q: Who makes the spectacles stay locked on?
options: Oz ordered it when the city was first built
questions.why: Keep an eye on the spectacles: the reason for them turns out to be very important later.

questions.q: Does Toto get spectacles?
options: Yes, even little Toto wears a pair
questions.why: Everyone in the group is given a pair, Toto included.

questions.q: What might a careful reader suspect from the rule about spectacles?
options: The green brightness might have more to do with the spectacles than with the city itself
questions.why: It's a hint that things in the Emerald City may not be what they seem.

questions.q: What happens once everyone has spectacles on?
options: The Guardian puts on his own spectacles and leads them through another gate into the city
They are sent away until morning
questions.why: He takes a big golden key from a peg on the wall and opens another gate, and they follow him into the streets.

questions.q: What are the houses in the Emerald City built of?
options: Green marble studded with sparkling emeralds
questions.why: Even the window panes are green glass, and the sky has a green tint.

questions.q: What is unusual about the things for sale in the city?
options: Everything is green — green candy, green popcorn, green shoes and hats, even green lemonade
They are all made of gold
questions.why: The children even pay for their green lemonade with green pennies.

questions.q: What does Dorothy notice about how the people move goods around?
options: There are no horses or animals; men carry things in little green carts they push in front of them
questions.why: The people look happy, contented and prosperous.

questions.q: Who takes the travelers' message to Oz?
options: A soldier in a green uniform with a long green beard
questions.why: He is called the Soldier with the Green Whiskers, and he returns with Oz's answer.

questions.q: What is Oz's rule for seeing the travelers?
options: Each must come alone, and he will see only one each day
questions.why: This means it takes four days for all four friends to see him.

questions.q: Which of these is in Dorothy's room at the palace?
options: A fountain that sprays green perfume into the air
questions.why: Her room also has green silk sheets and a wardrobe full of green dresses.

questions.q: What does the Throne Room look like?
options: A big round room with a high arched roof, its walls, ceiling and floor covered with large emeralds
questions.why: A great light as bright as the sun shines in the center of the roof.

questions.q: What form does Oz take when Dorothy sees him?
options: An enormous Head with no body, arms or legs
questions.why: The Head sits on a green marble throne, and its eyes move as it speaks.

questions.q: How does Oz introduce himself?
options: "I am Oz, the Great and Terrible"
"I am the King of the Emeralds"
"I am the Wizard of the West"
questions.why: His grand title is meant to fill visitors with awe.

questions.q: How does Dorothy introduce herself in reply?
options: "I am Dorothy, the Small and Meek"
questions.why: Her humble answer copies the style of his grand one.

questions.q: What two things does Oz ask Dorothy about?
options: Where she got the silver shoes and the mark on her forehead
questions.why: The shoes and the kiss mark are signs of power that even Oz takes seriously.

questions.q: What does Oz demand before he will help Dorothy?
options: That she kill the Wicked Witch of the West
questions.why: He says that when she can tell him the Witch is dead, he will send her home — but not before.

questions.q: How does Dorothy respond to Oz's demand?
options: She says she has never killed anything willingly, and she cries
questions.why: She knows she is only a little girl and is heartbroken.

questions.q: What form does Oz take for the Scarecrow?
options: A lovely Lady with gauzy wings
questions.why: She wears green silk gauze and a crown of jewels.

questions.q: What does Oz promise the Scarecrow if the Witch is killed?
options: So many good brains that he'll be the wisest man in Oz
questions.why: Oz sets the same price for every traveler.

questions.q: How is the Beast that the Tin Woodman sees described?
options: Nearly as big as an elephant, with a head like a rhinoceros and five eyes, five arms and five legs
questions.why: The Tin Woodman isn't afraid, since he believes he has no heart to feel fear.

questions.q: What form does Oz take for the Lion?
questions.why: The fire is so hot that it singes his whiskers and he backs away.

questions.q: What does Oz tell the Lion to bring him?
options: Proof that the Wicked Witch is dead
questions.why: Only then, Oz says, will he give the Lion courage.

questions.q: What pattern do you notice in Oz's answers to all four travelers?
options: He gives each a different task
He gives every one of them the same task: kill the Wicked Witch of the West
questions.why: The repeated demand is a clue that Oz can't solve the problem himself.

questions.q: How does the chapter end?
options: They decide to go to the land of the Winkies and look for the Wicked Witch
questions.why: Though they are frightened, they have no other way to get what they want.

chapters.title: 12. The Search for the Wicked Witch

questions.q: What does the Guardian do before the travelers leave the city?
options: Unlocks and removes their green spectacles
questions.why: He puts the spectacles back in his great box.

questions.q: What does the Guardian say about the road to the Wicked Witch?
options: There is no road, because no one ever wishes to go that way
questions.why: He tells them to keep to the West, where the sun sets.

questions.q: What do they discover about Dorothy's green silk dress once they are outside the city?
questions.why: This is another strong clue that the 'green' city is not quite what it seems.

questions.q: How does the Wicked Witch of the West see the travelers coming?
options: She has only one eye, but it is as powerful as a telescope and can see everywhere
questions.why: She spots them from the door of her castle.

questions.q: What does the Witch use to call her creatures?
options: A silver whistle she wears around her neck
questions.why: She blows it to call her wolves and her crows.

questions.q: Who defeats the forty wolves?
options: The Tin Woodman, with his axe
questions.why: The Woodman says this is his fight, and he kills them one by one as they come.

questions.q: How does the Scarecrow handle the forty crows?
options: He catches each one by the head and twists its neck
questions.why: The crows aren't afraid of him at first, but they are wrong.

questions.q: How do they protect Dorothy, Toto and the Lion from the black bees?
options: The Scarecrow's straw is scattered over them
questions.why: The Scarecrow's quick idea saves the ones who can be stung.

questions.q: What happens to the bees?
options: They break their stings on the Tin Woodman and die
They fly back to the Witch
questions.why: Bees can't live when their stings are broken, so the attack fails.

questions.q: How does the Lion drive off the Winkies the Witch sends?
options: By giving a great roar and springing toward them
questions.why: The frightened Winkies run back to the castle.

questions.q: How many times can the owner of the Golden Cap call the Winged Monkeys?
options: As many times as they like
questions.why: The Witch has already used it twice, so this is her last call.

questions.q: What had the Witch used the Golden Cap for before?
options: To build her castle and find gold
To catch Dorothy and the Lion
To make the Winkies her slaves, and to drive Oz out of the land of the West
questions.why: Knowing the cap's history explains why Oz fears her.

questions.q: What do the Winged Monkeys do to the Tin Woodman?
options: Drop him onto sharp rocks, where he lies battered and dented
questions.why: He is left unable to move or groan.

questions.q: What do the Monkeys do to the Scarecrow?
options: Pull the straw out of his clothes and head and throw his hat, boots and clothes into the top of a tall tree
questions.why: Without his straw, he is just an empty bundle of clothes.

questions.q: Why don't the Winged Monkeys harm Dorothy?
options: She has the mark of the Good Witch's kiss, and she is protected by the Power of Good, which is greater than the Power of Evil
questions.why: The Monkey King says they dare not harm her, so they carry her gently to the castle.

questions.q: Why is the Witch afraid when she sees Dorothy's silver shoes?
options: They could make Dorothy fly away
She knows they have a powerful charm
questions.why: Then she looks into Dorothy's eyes and sees that the girl doesn't know how to use their power.

questions.q: What does the Witch make Dorothy do?
options: Work in the kitchen — clean the pots and kettles, sweep the floor, and keep the fire fed with wood
Wash the Witch's clothes in the river
questions.why: Dorothy works hard, glad the Witch hasn't decided to kill her.

questions.q: How does Dorothy keep the Lion alive?
options: She secretly brings him food from the cupboard at night
She asks the Winkies to feed him
She gives him the Witch's dinner
questions.why: The Witch won't feed him until he agrees to be harnessed like a horse.

questions.q: How does the Witch get one of Dorothy's silver shoes?
options: She steals it while Dorothy sleeps
She trips Dorothy with an invisible iron bar, and a shoe comes off
She orders a Monkey to take it
questions.why: She is too afraid of the dark to sneak in at night and too afraid of water to take the shoes while Dorothy bathes.

questions.q: How is the Wicked Witch destroyed?
options: Dorothy, angry about her shoe, throws a bucket of water over her, and she melts
questions.why: Dorothy didn't know water would destroy the Witch. She was only angry.

questions.q: What is the first thing Dorothy does after the Witch melts?
options: Unlocks the gate of the Lion's prison and sets him free
questions.why: The Lion is delighted to learn the Witch was melted by a bucket of water.

questions.q: How do the Winkies celebrate their freedom?
options: They make the day a holiday, then and ever after
questions.why: They had been slaves of the Witch for many years.

questions.q: What color is the Winkies' country?
questions.why: Yellow is the Winkies' color, just as blue belongs to the Munchkins.

questions.q: Who helps Dorothy search for her lost friends?
questions.why: Dorothy and the Lion ask the Winkies to help rescue the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman.

questions.q: How is the Tin Woodman found?
options: Lying on the rocky plain, battered and bent, with his axe rusted and its handle broken
questions.why: The Winkies carry him back to the castle.

questions.q: Who repairs the Tin Woodman?
questions.why: They work on him for three days and four nights.

questions.q: How does the Tin Woodman look after he is repaired?
options: Patched in some places, but able to move as well as ever
questions.why: He doesn't mind the patches at all.

questions.q: What do the Winkies do to the Tin Woodman's axe?
options: Give it a new handle of gold and polish the blade
questions.why: His axe comes back better than before.

questions.q: Why does Dorothy wipe the Tin Woodman's tears carefully with her apron?
options: So no one sees him cry
questions.why: He weeps for joy at seeing his friends. Remember what happened after the beetle!

questions.q: Where are the Scarecrow's clothes found?
options: In the top of a very tall tree
questions.why: The tree is so tall and smooth that no one can climb it.

questions.q: How do they get the Scarecrow's clothes down?
options: The Tin Woodman chops the tree down
questions.why: The Woodman's axe solves the problem again.

questions.q: How is the Scarecrow restored?
options: He wakes up on his own
His clothes are stuffed with nice, clean straw
questions.why: He is soon as good as ever, and he thanks everyone.

questions.q: Why does Dorothy want to go back to the Emerald City?
options: To claim the promises Oz made them
questions.why: Now that the Witch is gone, it's time for Oz to keep his word.

questions.q: What gift do Toto and the Lion receive?
questions.why: The Winkies give each traveler a gift.

questions.q: What does Dorothy receive from the Winkies?
options: A beautiful bracelet studded with diamonds
questions.why: Each gift matches the person receiving it.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow receive?
options: A gold-headed walking stick, to keep him from stumbling
questions.why: It is a thoughtful gift for someone who keeps falling over.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman receive?
options: A silver oil-can, inlaid with gold and set with precious jewels
questions.why: It is the perfect gift for a man who rusts.

questions.q: Where does Dorothy find the Golden Cap?
options: In the Witch's cupboard, when she goes to fill her basket with food
questions.why: She doesn't know it is magic. She thinks it is pretty and it fits her.

questions.q: Why does Dorothy decide to wear the Golden Cap?
options: She knows it controls the Monkeys
It is pretty and it fits her exactly, so she wears it and puts her sunbonnet in the basket
questions.why: She has a powerful object without knowing it — just like the silver shoes.

questions.q: What does this chapter show about the Winkies?
options: They are grateful and generous to the people who freed them
questions.why: Their care and gifts show how thankful they are.

questions.q: Why do the travelers get lost on the way back?
options: There is no road, and they can't keep heading east once the sun is overhead
A storm blows them off course
questions.why: They know to walk toward the rising sun, but by midday they can't tell east from west.

questions.q: What do they walk through for days?
options: Great fields of buttercups and yellow daisies
questions.why: Without landmarks, the fields all look the same.

questions.q: How does the Lion feel after days of walking?
options: He whimpers that he doesn't have the courage to keep tramping forever without getting anywhere
questions.why: Everyone is tired and discouraged.

questions.q: How does Dorothy call the field mice?
options: She blows the little whistle the Queen of the Mice gave her
questions.why: The Queen and her mice arrive quickly.

questions.q: What does the Queen of the Mice suggest?
options: Using the charm of the Golden Cap to call the Winged Monkeys
questions.why: The Queen knows what the cap can do, even though Dorothy doesn't.

questions.q: Where does Dorothy find the magic words?
options: Written inside the lining of the Golden Cap
questions.why: The instructions tell her exactly what to say and how to stand.

questions.q: What does Dorothy say while standing on her left foot?
questions.why: Then she says 'Hil-lo, hol-lo, hel-lo!' on her right foot, and 'Ziz-zy, zuz-zy, zik!' standing on both feet.

questions.q: What does Dorothy say while standing on both feet?
questions.why: The third part of the charm brings the Monkeys.

questions.q: What does Dorothy ask the Monkeys to do?
options: Carry them to the Emerald City
questions.why: This is Dorothy's first use of the cap.

questions.q: How had the Winged Monkeys lived long ago?
options: As a free people, living happily in the great forest, flying from tree to tree and eating nuts and fruit
questions.why: The Monkey King tells their history as they fly.

questions.q: Who was Gayelette?
options: The Wicked Witch of the West
A beautiful princess who was also a powerful sorceress
questions.why: She lived in a handsome palace built of great blocks of ruby.

questions.q: What prank did the Monkey King's grandfather play?
options: He set the palace on fire
He had the Monkeys drop the richly dressed Quelala into the river
questions.why: The Monkeys were full of mischief, and this joke got them into deep trouble.

questions.q: What did Gayelette first want to do to the Monkeys as punishment?
options: Tie their wings and throw them into the river
questions.why: She wanted to treat them the way they had treated Quelala.

questions.q: What punishment did the Monkeys receive in the end?
options: They must obey the owner of the Golden Cap three times
They were sent to the desert
They had to serve Gayelette forever
questions.why: The grandfather pleaded, and this was the price for sparing them.

questions.q: How did the Golden Cap come to the Wicked Witch of the West?
options: She got hold of it after it had passed from its earlier owner
questions.why: The Monkey King explains that she then used it to make them do her will.

questions.q: What does the Monkey King's story teach about the Monkeys' earlier acts?
options: They acted by their own choice
They were bound by the cap to obey whoever owned it, not acting from their own wickedness
questions.why: This helps explain why the Monkeys now treat Dorothy kindly.

questions.q: How do the Monkeys carry Dorothy?
questions.why: Monkeys carry each traveler, and Dorothy rides safely.

questions.q: Where do the Monkeys set the travelers down?
options: At the gate of the Emerald City
questions.why: Then the Monkeys bow to Dorothy and fly away.

questions.q: How many calls on the Golden Cap does Dorothy have left after this chapter?
questions.why: Dorothy has used one of her three calls.

questions.q: What mistake about power does the prank story warn against?
options: Playing cruel jokes, which can have serious consequences
questions.why: A single piece of mischief cost the Monkeys their freedom.

chapters.title: 15. The Discovery of Oz, the Terrible

questions.q: What happens after the travelers tell the palace that they have returned?
options: Days go by with no word from Oz
questions.why: They expect to be called right away, but Oz keeps them waiting.

questions.q: How does the Scarecrow finally get Oz to see them?
options: He sends word that they'll call the Winged Monkeys if Oz doesn't keep his promises
He asks the Guardian for help
questions.why: Oz has met the Monkeys before and doesn't want to meet them again.

questions.q: At what time are they told to come to the Throne Room?
options: Four minutes after nine the next morning
questions.why: The oddly exact time is a small, funny detail.

questions.q: What do they see when they enter the Throne Room together?
questions.why: A voice seems to come from somewhere near the top of the great dome.

questions.q: What does the voice claim about where Oz is?
options: That he is everywhere, but invisible to the eyes of ordinary people
questions.why: He is still trying to keep up the act.

questions.q: How does Oz react when told the Witch was melted?
options: He keeps his promises at once
He asks them to come back tomorrow so he can think it over
questions.why: His delay makes the travelers angry.

questions.q: What causes the screen in the corner to fall over?
options: Toto jumps away in alarm when the Lion roars and tips it over
questions.why: Little Toto reveals the truth.

questions.q: Who is standing behind the screen?
options: A little old man with a bald head and a wrinkled face
questions.why: He looks as surprised as they are.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow call the little old man?
questions.why: The man agrees: 'Exactly so! I am a humbug.'

questions.q: Where was the Wizard born?
questions.why: Dorothy points out that Omaha isn't very far from Kansas.

questions.q: What skill helped the Wizard fake Oz's voice?
options: He was a ventriloquist, so he could throw his voice
questions.why: He learned it from a great master and could make his voice seem to come from anywhere.

questions.q: What was the Wizard's job before he came to Oz?
options: A balloonist who went up on circus day to draw a crowd
questions.why: One day his balloon's ropes got twisted, and he couldn't come down.

questions.q: Why did the people of Oz believe he was a great Wizard?
options: They saw him come down from the clouds
questions.why: He let them believe it, because they were afraid of him and promised to do whatever he wished.

questions.q: Why did the Wizard make everyone wear green spectacles?
options: To make the name 'Emerald City' fit better — everything looks green through them
questions.why: The city is really no greener than any other city.

questions.q: How did the Wizard make the Great Head?
options: Out of many layers of paper, with a painted face, moved by strings
questions.why: He hung it from the ceiling by a wire and pulled strings to move its eyes and mouth.

questions.q: What was the Ball of Fire?
options: A ball of cotton soaked in oil and set on fire
questions.why: Each of Oz's 'forms' was a trick.

questions.q: Why had the Wizard lived in fear for so many years?
options: He feared the Wicked Witches would destroy him if they learned he had no real power
questions.why: That's why he was so glad when Dorothy's house fell on the Witch of the East.

questions.q: How does the Wizard answer when Dorothy calls him a very bad man?
options: "I'm really a very good man, but I'm a very bad Wizard"
"I am the greatest man in Oz"
questions.why: He admits to being a fake, but not to being wicked.

questions.q: What does the Wizard tell the Lion about courage?
options: It can only come from a bottle
True courage is facing danger when you are afraid, and the Lion has plenty of it
questions.why: This is one of the book's central ideas about courage.

questions.q: What does the Wizard tell the Scarecrow about knowledge?
options: Only Oz can make him wise
He is learning something every day, and only experience brings knowledge
questions.why: The Scarecrow still wants brains, so the Wizard agrees to give him some.

chapters.title: 16. The Magic Art of the Great Humbug

questions.q: Who goes to Oz first to receive his gift?
questions.why: He tells his friends to congratulate him, since he is going to get his brains at last.

questions.q: What does Oz do first to the Scarecrow?
options: Takes off his head and empties out the straw
questions.why: It's a little alarming, but the Scarecrow doesn't mind.

questions.q: What does Oz use for the Scarecrow's 'brains'?
options: A measure of bran mixed with many pins and needles
questions.why: Oz makes a pun on the word 'bran.'

questions.q: What pun does Oz make?
questions.why: 'Bran-new' sounds like 'brand-new.'

questions.q: What does the Lion say the pins and needles sticking out of the Scarecrow's head prove?
questions.why: 'Sharp' is another pun — it means clever.

questions.q: How does the Scarecrow feel after receiving his brains?
questions.why: He believes in the brains, and that belief makes him confident.

questions.q: What tool does Oz use to open the Tin Woodman's chest?
questions.why: He cuts a small square hole in the left side of the Woodman's breast.

questions.q: What is the Tin Woodman's heart made of?
questions.why: It's a pretty heart, but not a real one.

questions.q: What question does the Tin Woodman ask about his new heart?
questions.why: What he cares about most is kindness, which he has shown all along.

questions.q: How does Oz close the hole in the Tin Woodman's chest?
options: He puts back the square of tin and solders it
questions.why: Oz apologizes that he had to put a patch on the Woodman's breast.

questions.q: What does Oz pour the Lion's courage from?
questions.why: He pours it into a beautifully carved green-gold dish.

questions.q: How does the Lion react to the dish at first?
options: He sniffs at it as if he doesn't like it
questions.why: Oz tells him to drink.

questions.q: How does Oz explain why the Lion must drink it?
options: Courage is always inside one, so it can't be called courage until it's swallowed
questions.why: The explanation is clever word play, not magic.

questions.q: How does the Lion say he feels after drinking?
questions.why: Like the others, he gets what he believes in.

questions.q: What does Oz say makes it hard for him to stop being a humbug?
options: People keep making him do things that everybody knows can't be done
questions.why: He blames the demands of others for his pretending.

questions.q: Why was it easy for Oz to make the three friends happy?
options: They imagined he could do anything
questions.why: Their belief did most of the work.

questions.q: What does Oz admit will take more than imagination?
questions.why: Dorothy's wish is the one he can't fake.

questions.q: What is the book suggesting about the three gifts?
options: The friends already had brains, a heart and courage, and the gifts helped them believe it
questions.why: Each friend showed these qualities long before reaching Oz.

questions.q: What does the word 'humbug' mean?
options: A fake or fraud who pretends to be something he isn't
questions.why: The chapter title calls Oz 'the Great Humbug.'

questions.q: How is the Tin Woodman's reaction to his heart different from the Scarecrow's to his brains?
options: He focuses on whether it's kind and is deeply grateful
questions.why: The Scarecrow cares about being wise. The Woodman cares about being good to others.

questions.q: How does Dorothy feel during the three days of waiting?
options: Sad, because she hears nothing from Oz
questions.why: Her friends are all happy with their gifts, which makes her feel more alone.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman say about his new heart?
options: It is kinder and more tender than the one he had when he was made of flesh
questions.why: He can feel it rattling around in his chest.

questions.q: What does the Lion now say he could face?
options: An army or a dozen of the fierce Kalidahs
questions.why: His new belief in himself changes how he talks.

questions.q: How does Oz think Dorothy can cross the desert?
options: Through the air, in a balloon
questions.why: He came to Oz through the air, and so did Dorothy.

questions.q: Why can't Oz fill the balloon with gas?
options: There is no gas in all this country
questions.why: He must use hot air instead.

questions.q: What is the danger of using hot air?
options: If the air cools, the balloon could come down in the desert
It makes the balloon too fast
questions.why: Hot air isn't as good as gas.

questions.q: Why does Oz want to go with Dorothy?
options: He wants to see Aunt Em
He is tired of being a humbug and shut up in the palace, and would like to be in a circus again
He is afraid of the Scarecrow
questions.why: If he left the palace, the people would find out that he isn't a Wizard.

questions.q: What is the balloon made of?
options: Strips of green silk sewn together
questions.why: The bag is more than twenty feet long when it is finished.

questions.q: How long does it take to sew the balloon?
questions.why: Dorothy helps sew the strips together.

questions.q: How does Oz make the balloon airtight?
options: He paints the inside with a coat of thin glue
questions.why: Careful work, not magic, makes the balloon.

questions.q: What does Oz use for the balloon's basket?
questions.why: He sends the soldier to fetch it and ties it to the bottom of the balloon.

questions.q: What reason does Oz give the people for his trip?
options: He is going home to Omaha
He is going to fight a witch
He is going to visit a great brother Wizard who lives in the clouds
questions.why: He keeps up the act to the very end.

questions.q: Who fills the balloon with hot air?
options: The Tin Woodman chops wood for a fire, and Oz holds the balloon over it
questions.why: The hot air rising from the fire is caught in the silk bag.

questions.q: Who does Oz leave in charge of the Emerald City?
questions.why: He tells the people to obey the Scarecrow as they would obey him.

questions.q: Why isn't Dorothy in the basket when the balloon rises?
options: Toto runs into the crowd to bark at a kitten, and she goes to get him
questions.why: Once again, going after Toto changes everything — just as in the cyclone.

questions.q: What happens just as Dorothy runs back with Toto?
options: The ropes break, and the balloon rises without her
questions.why: She is only a few steps away when it happens.

questions.q: What are Oz's last words to Dorothy?
options: "I can't come back, my dear. Good-bye!"
questions.why: Then the balloon floats away into the sky.

questions.q: What does the narrator say might have happened to Oz?
options: He may have reached Omaha safely, for all we know
questions.why: His ending is left open.

questions.q: How do the people remember Oz?
options: As always their friend, who built them the beautiful Emerald City
questions.why: They never learn that he was a humbug.

questions.q: How does this chapter connect to Chapter 1?
options: Dorothy is angry at Toto both times
In both, Dorothy's choice to go after Toto keeps her from getting away in time
questions.why: Her loyalty to Toto costs her a way out — twice.

questions.q: How does Dorothy feel after the balloon leaves?
options: She cries bitterly about losing her chance to get home, though she's glad she didn't go up in it
questions.why: She is sorry to lose her chance to go home, but glad she did not go up in the balloon.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman ask before crying for Oz?
options: That Dorothy wipe away his tears so he won't rust
questions.why: Dorothy brings a towel. He's grateful to the man who gave him his heart.

questions.q: Who now rules the Emerald City?
questions.why: The people are proud to be ruled by a stuffed man.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow marvel at as ruler?
options: That a short time ago he was stuck on a pole in a farmer's cornfield
questions.why: His rise is a big change from where he started.

questions.q: Why won't Dorothy stay and live in the Emerald City?
options: She wants to go to Kansas and live with Aunt Em and Uncle Henry
She is afraid of the people
The Scarecrow asks her to leave
questions.why: Her goal hasn't changed since Chapter 2.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow suggest after thinking hard?
options: Calling the Winged Monkeys to carry Dorothy over the desert
Asking the Witch of the North
questions.why: He thinks so hard that the pins and needles stick out of his brains.

questions.q: Why can't the Winged Monkeys take Dorothy to Kansas?
options: They are afraid of Aunt Em
They belong to this country alone and cannot leave it
questions.why: The Monkey King says there has never been a Winged Monkey in Kansas.

questions.q: How many times has Dorothy now used the Golden Cap?
questions.why: The Monkey King points out that this is the second time she has called them, so she has one call left.

questions.q: How does Dorothy feel about this use of the cap?
options: That she wasted its charm for nothing
questions.why: The limit of three makes each wish precious.

questions.q: Who does the Scarecrow ask for advice next?
options: The Soldier with the Green Whiskers
questions.why: The soldier knows about the lands beyond the city.

questions.q: Who does the soldier suggest might help Dorothy?
options: Glinda, the Witch of the South
questions.why: He says Glinda is the most powerful of all the Witches.

questions.q: Who does Glinda rule?
questions.why: The Quadlings live in the South.

questions.q: Why might Glinda know how to cross the desert?
options: Her castle stands on the edge of the desert
questions.why: Living so near the desert, she might know a way across.

questions.q: What dangers does the soldier warn about on the road south?
options: Wild beasts in the woods, and a race of queer men who don't like strangers
questions.why: Because of these dangers, the Quadlings never come to the Emerald City.

questions.q: Why does the Lion want to go south with Dorothy?
options: He is afraid to stay alone
He is tired of the city and longs for the woods, and Dorothy will need protection
questions.why: He says he is really a wild beast.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman offer Dorothy?
options: His axe, which may be of use to her
questions.why: He decides to go with her to the Land of the South.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow insist on going too, even though he is now ruler?
options: Without Dorothy he would never have had brains, so his good luck is all thanks to her
questions.why: He won't leave her until she has left for Kansas for good.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman say when the Scarecrow reaches his wise decision?
questions.why: It's a friendly joke about the Scarecrow's new brains.

questions.q: When do they decide to leave?
questions.why: The chapter ends with the plan made.

questions.q: What does this chapter show about the three friends?
options: They are selfish now that they got their wishes
They are afraid of the South
Even after getting what they wanted, they stay loyal to Dorothy
questions.why: Each friend risks danger to help her get home.

questions.q: What does Dorothy do the morning they leave the city?
options: She kisses the pretty green girl good-bye
questions.why: They also shake hands with the soldier, who walks with them to the gate.

questions.q: What does the Guardian tell the Scarecrow?
options: That he is now their ruler, so he must come back as soon as possible
questions.why: The Guardian unlocks their spectacles and puts them back in the box.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman say about Oz as they look back at the city?
options: Oz was not such a bad Wizard, after all
questions.why: He feels his new heart rattling in his chest as he says it.

questions.q: What does the Lion say about Oz?
options: That if Oz had taken a dose of the courage he gave the Lion, he would have been a brave man
questions.why: It's a joke with a kind edge.

questions.q: How does Dorothy feel about Oz?
options: She forgives him, because he did his best, and he was a good man even if a bad Wizard
She thinks he tricked her on purpose
questions.why: Dorothy's forgiveness shows her kind heart.

questions.q: Where do the travelers sleep the first night?
options: On the grass, with nothing above them but the stars
questions.why: They rest well even outdoors.

questions.q: What do they come to on the second day?
options: A thick wood that stretches as far as they can see
questions.why: They can't go around it without losing their way.

questions.q: What happens when the Scarecrow tries to walk under the first trees?
options: The branches bend down, wrap around him, and fling him back
questions.why: The trees don't let strangers pass.

questions.q: How many times is the Scarecrow thrown back?
questions.why: He tries a second opening between the trees and is thrown out again.

questions.q: Who solves the problem of the fighting trees?
options: The Tin Woodman, who chops a grabbing branch in two
questions.why: The whole tree shakes as if in pain, and the Woodman walks safely under it.

questions.q: What happens to Toto?
options: He is caught by a small branch and shaken until he howls, then freed by the Woodman
He is thrown over the wall
questions.why: The Woodman cuts the branch and sets Toto free.

questions.q: What do the travelers decide about the fighting trees?
options: All the trees in the forest can fight
The trees are under a witch's spell
Only the first row can bend their branches — perhaps they are the forest's 'policemen,' meant to keep strangers out
questions.why: The trees farther in don't try to stop them.

questions.q: What do they find at the far edge of the woods?
options: A high wall that seems to be made of white china
questions.why: It is smooth like the surface of a dish, and higher than their heads.

questions.q: Who offers to build a ladder to get over the wall?
questions.why: The chapter ends with this plan.

questions.q: What pattern keeps showing up in how the group solves problems?
options: Each friend uses his own strengths — the Woodman's axe often clears the way
questions.why: Teamwork and each friend's skills get them through.

questions.q: Why can't the Scarecrow be hurt by the fighting trees?
options: He is stuffed with straw and can't be hurt, though he is surprised
questions.why: The trees throw him down, but he isn't hurt — only surprised.

questions.q: What word best describes the Tin Woodman in this chapter?
questions.why: He clears the way and rescues Toto.

questions.q: What does the Guardian say to Dorothy when she says goodbye?
options: That they would like to keep her, but he hopes she finds a way if she wants to go to Kansas
questions.why: Even the Guardian cares about her.

questions.q: What do the friends' comments about Oz show?
options: They didn't know he was a humbug
They are grateful to him even though they know he was a humbug
questions.why: Knowing the truth doesn't take away their thanks.

questions.q: Which word best fits the mood as they leave the Emerald City?
